native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project (ee) are substantially longer than those in the Psychology project (rpp): ee originals average 28.0 pages (n=18) versus 11.2 pages for rpp originals (n=97), i.e., roughly 2.5× longer. Length is measured in pages per the schema ('length' = number of pages of original paper).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded the 927-row meta-regression study data CSV with pandas. Filtered to project=='ee' (18 rows) and project=='rpp' (97 rows). Verified 'length' (pages of original paper, per schema) is fully numeric with 0 missing, 0 zero/negative, and max 45 — no invalid values, so no rows were excluded. Computed the per-row arithmetic mean of 'length' per project: ee = 28.00 (n=18), rpp = 11.22 (n=97), ratio 2.50. Computed sensitivity excluding drop=True rows (rpp: 11.00, n=90; ee unaffected, no drop=True rows) and a per-unique-paper robustness variant (rpp: 11.23, n=95; ee unchanged). The second dataset was not used (it has no length column).
